newsitem.title: INDIA: Dow Chemical Co plans PET unit in India.
newsitem.headline: Dow Chemical Co plans PET unit in India.

text.p: Dow Chemical Co of the U.S. is sending a team to India to study the feasibility of setting up a PET (polyethylene terephthalate) plant, H.S. Ranka, chairman of India's Modern Group said on Monday.
PET is a plastic resin used by the packaging industry.
The Dow team is arriving in India on September 17 for discussions with group firm Modern Syntex, Ranka told reporters. The 50,000 tonnes per annum plant would cost about 5.0 billion rupees, he said.
The Modern Group has over 10 billion rupees turnover in various segments of the textile industry.

Another group firm Modern Threads is building a 16.6 billion rupee plant to manufacture polyester raw material purified terephthalic acid (PTA) in technical collaboration with Inca International Spa, a Dow Chemical subsidiary.
Polyester chips produced by Modern Threads' PTA plant will be the raw material for the PET project.
Ranka said Dow suggested the diversification. "We are interested only if there is a 100 percent buyback (by Dow)," he said.
Indian polyester leader Reliance Industries is building a 80,000 tonnes per annum PET project in western India.
